First, we write the integral as

$$
\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{2x+1} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{2x}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use a substitution $2x+1=u,$ thus $2x=u-1$ and $\text{d}x=\frac{\text{d}u}{2}.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{3}⁡(2x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int (\frac{2x}{2x+1})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\int \frac{u-1}{u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{1}{2}\int \,\text{d}u+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{u}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{u}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡u}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-\frac{2x+1}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2}+D] \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{(2x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+1)-2x}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=D-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}$ is an integral constant.
